_README: Contract breaches the read-only integration suite commits when replayed
against the fake. This is a RATCHET, asserted exactly: a NEW entry fails
CI, and so does a STALE one, so a fix has to be recorded here as well.
An entry is a call the suite makes that the endpoint catalog
(tests/endpoints.json) does not support. Against a live Ghidra each one
still returns HTTP 200 -- the plugin ignores parameters it does not
declare -- so the test passes while asserting nothing about the thing its
name claims. That is why they were invisible until an offline run had a
catalog to check against.
THE LIST IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE POINT.
W12 / issue #112 discovered ten of these on 2026-08-30 and recorded them
here rather than changing what a test asserts. All ten were fixed on
2026-08-30 (see CHANGELOG 'read-only suite contract breaches'): parameter
names corrected, one GET turned out to be a POST mutator and left the
read-only tier, three tests called endpoints that do not exist, and one
-- /get_function_labels sent `address` -- was never a breach at all: it
is a declared @Param alias the schema simply does not advertise.
Keep it empty. Adding a line here is a decision to ship a test that
cannot fail, and it is now the SECOND line of defence in any case:
tests/unit/test_integration_call_contract.py checks every integration
file statically, needs no fixtures, and runs in the unit tier that CI
always executes.
